digest.en: Gunmen killed 24 people in coordinated attacks across Nigeria. Meanwhile, UK PM Burnham blames Iran’s IRGC for the RAF Fairford incident. These simultaneous shocks test regional security architectures.
digest.hi: लंदन में ब्रिटिश पीएम का दावा है कि ईरान ने एयरबेस हमले की साजिश रची थी। इसी वक्त रियाद में सऊदी अरब होतियों से बदले की तैयारी कर रहा है। तेल की गलियों में तनाव और भी गहरा हो गया है।

articles.title: Gunmen kill 24 in Nigerian attacks
articles.summary: Armed groups killed 24 people in recent attacks across two Nigerian regions. The violence is attributed to local bandits and jihadist factions. These groups target communities for ransom and cattle theft. The incident highlights the ongoing instability in the area. There has been a recent increase in attacks on communities in the two regions, blamed on gangs engaged in kidnapping for ransom and cattle rustling.

articles.title: France braces for fresh student demonstrations as Macron calls for ‘respect’
articles.summary: French students blocked hundreds of high schools since late September. They protest poor classroom conditions and demand better resources. Riot police are deployed at entrances. President Macron has called for respect during the ongoing demonstrations. Students have blocked entrances to hundreds of lycees. high schools for children 15 to 18. since late September to rail against poor classroom conditions, with squads of riot police deployed and occasionally violent clashes erupting.

articles.title: U.K. PM Burnham says Iran’s IRGC likely behind RAF Fairford incident
articles.summary: U. K. Prime Minister Burnham stated the IRGC likely caused the RAF Fairford incident. The base hosted U. S. bombers striking Iran. President Trump said an Iran-linked threat forced the planes out. The base remains a key location for allied operations. The RAF ⁠Fairfordbase had been used by U. S. bombers to carry out strikes on Iran but last week, U. S. President Donald Trump said a ‌threat linked to Iran had prompted the removal of the planes.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says Yandex Strikes Crippled Pro-Kremlin Bots But Tech Experts Question Evidence
articles.summary: Zelenskyy claimed Ukraine’s strikes on Yandex data centers reduced pro-Kremlin bots. He said the attacks crippled the network. Tech experts dispute this assessment. They question the evidence linking the strikes to a drop in bot activity. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that Ukraine's recent attacks on Russian tech giant Yandex’s data centers have resulted in fewer Internet bots promoting pro-Kremlin hate, a claim that has been disputed by many technology researchers.

articles.title: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection is buckling under cuts
articles.summary: UNHCR chief Barham Salih warned refugee protection is failing. The agency received only three billion dollars of its eight billion dollar need. One hundred seventeen million people are currently displaced. Funding gaps threaten the global asylum support system. The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year – and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

articles.title: Balkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for Greece
articles.summary: High pressure over the Balkans created sharp temperature swings in Montenegro. Daytime highs rose significantly while overnight lows dropped. A low-pressure system now moves toward the Aegean Sea. Heavy rain is expected to reach Greece soon. articles.title: One freed American doesn’t equal US policy shift on Myanmar
articles.summary: The United States opened direct talks with Myanmar’s military junta. This follows the release of an American citizen. The move reverses years of diplomatic isolation. It does not signal a victory for the generals or a defeat for the revolution. The recent Reuters headline, “US opens direct talks with Myanmar’s generals, reversing years of isolation,” describes a consequential diplomatic change.

articles.title: Houthi Riyadh airport hit shows Saudi air defenses full of holes
articles.summary: Houthi forces struck Riyadh airport using suicide drones, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles. The attack lasted about 45 minutes starting at 3 PM local time. The mixed-speed weapons overwhelmed Saudi air defenses. The strike exposed significant gaps in the kingdom's defensive network. The Houthi attack mixed together suicide drones, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles. Because these weapons travel at significantly different speeds, the drones were launched first, followed by the cruise missiles and lastly by the ballistic missiles.

articles.title: When AI takes control of weapons systems
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is expanding into national defense systems. Machine learning now handles reconnaissance, early warning, and target detection. These tools promise faster analysis and decision-making. However, AI exacerbates existing security problems that cannot be solved technically. Artificial intelligence is rapidly making its way into national defense. Reconnaissance, early warning, target detection, mission planning. everywhere, machine-learning systems promise faster analysis, faster responses, and faster decision-making.

articles.title: China fast on Ukraine lessons, slow on command reform
articles.summary: China is rapidly modernizing its defenses using lessons from the Russia-Ukraine war. However, its centralized command structure struggles with decentralized modern combat demands. A CSIS report highlights this friction. The war serves as a real-time laboratory for Chinese military adaptation. The Russia-Ukraine War has become a real-time laboratory for the Chinese military, spurring rapid defensive modernization while exposing deep friction between its centralized command hierarchy and the decentralized demands of modern combat.

articles.title: Is Modi facing his own Bangladesh moment?
articles.summary: Demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner is a severe political challenge for Prime Minister Modi. Unlike sacrificing a minister, this move threatens the government's legitimacy. The situation mirrors a potential Bangladesh moment. The pressure on the prime minister is significant. Demanding the resignation of a minister is one thing. It is uncomfortable for a government, occasionally embarrassing for a prime minister, but ultimately manageable.

articles.title: US-China race is on for the Gulf’s AI future
articles.summary: Chinese AI and digital infrastructure investments in Saudi Arabia and the UAE are colliding with a larger American technology presence. Beijing offers cloud platforms, 5G networks, and surveillance systems at lower costs. This competition shapes the Gulf’s long-term digital sovereignty and strategic alignment. China’s artificial intelligence and digital-infrastructure investments in the Gulf Arab states are increasingly colliding with a far larger and more strategically privileged American technology presence, particularly in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

articles.title: Thousands without power in Florida and Alabama as Isaias moves north
articles.summary: Hurricane Isaias moved north on Sunday, leaving nearly 396,000 customers without power across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama. The storm brought moderate to heavy rainfall to the central Appalachians and mid-Atlantic region. Authorities issued warnings for flash flooding that could extend into the Appalachian mountains. At least four deaths have been linked to the storm so far. Heavy rainfall associated with the storm.

articles.title: Trump Announces Energy Cease-Fire Between Ukraine, Russia As Countries Trade Strikes
articles.summary: Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy cease-fire. This follows his decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports. He also called for a change in leadership in Kyiv. The two countries continued trading strikes during this period. US President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy cease-fire, following his earlier decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports and his subsequent call for a change in leadership in Kyiv.

articles.title: Missing Australian hiker Jordan Yap last seen on remote trail found dead in Peru
articles.summary: Jordan Yap, a 30-year-old Melbourne man, has been found dead in Peru after disappearing on a remote hiking trail. He last contacted friends while trekking in the South American country. His family and friends are remembering him for the immense joy he brought to their lives. The discovery ends a search for the Australian hiker who vanished during his trip.

articles.title: As Russian Arms Exports Slide, Central Asia Shops Elsewhere
articles.summary: Central Asian states are shifting military procurement away from Russia toward India, China, Turkey, and Europe. This diversification grants them greater political flexibility in negotiations with Moscow. Analysts warn that mixing equipment from multiple suppliers creates long-term logistical and operational challenges. The shift reflects a strategic move to reduce reliance on a single arms supplier. Central Asian nations are increasingly turning to India, China, Turkey, and Europe for military equipment to reduce their dependence on Russia.

articles.title: House Republicans Move To Block Trump's Russia Diesel Deal
articles.summary: Representative Brian Fitzpatrick is forcing a House vote on legislation to block Russian oil purchases. This move directly challenges President Donald Trump's decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports. Lawmakers warn the policy shift could help finance Moscow's war against Ukraine. The procedural maneuver tests the limits of congressional authority over executive trade decisions. Republican Representative Brian Fitzpatrick plans to force a House vote on legislation blocking Russian oil purchases, challenging President Donald Trump's decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports as lawmakers warn the move could help finance Moscow's war against Ukraine.

articles.title: Cultivating peace in Côte d’Ivoire
articles.summary: Adam Ouattara and Makongo Traoré live on the edge of Torla village in Côte d’Ivoire. He herds cattle while she grows vegetables nearby. For years, the dry season pitted their two livelihoods against each other over scarce water resources. Adam Ouattara and Makongo Traoré have four children and a home on the edge of Torla village in Côte d’Ivoire. She grows vegetables on a small plot nearby.

articles.title: UN rights office urges release of ‘arbitrarily detained’ protesters
articles.summary: The UN human rights office expressed concern over mass detentions in India. Authorities arrested demonstrators, protest leaders, lawyers, and journalists before and during large-scale protests in Delhi on Saturday. The organization urged the immediate release of these arbitrarily detained individuals. The UN human rights office (OHCHR) has voiced concern over reports of mass detentions in India of demonstrators, protest leaders, civil society members, lawyers and journalists, before and during large-scale protests in Delhi on Saturday.

articles.title: In the Mekong Delta, a push to grow food with saltwater
articles.summary: Farming in Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta has traditionally relied on seasonal river floods. These floods carried freshwater and sediment across flat fields, supporting the country’s status as a top rice exporter. Farmers are now adapting to saltwater intrusion to maintain food production. For generations, farming in Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta has depended on a delicate bargain. The river flooded, retreated and flooded again, carrying freshwater and sediment across a flat landscape whose vast fields helped turn the country into one of the world’s leading rice exporters.

articles.title: Anduril’s plan to save US sub edge from China’s undersea surge
articles.summary: Anduril Industries will invest US$3.7 billion to build a software-defined shipyard. The facility aims to overhaul US submarine manufacturing capabilities. The project addresses urgent needs in naval industrial capacity within the Indo-Pacific region. A multibillion-dollar private initiative to overhaul US submarine manufacturing marks an urgent push to revitalize naval industrial capacity at a pivotal moment in the Indo-Pacific balance of power.

articles.title: Controversial vaccine trial touted by RFK Jr gets go-ahead in Guinea-Bissau
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau approved a trial withholding hepatitis B vaccines from newborns. Danish researchers will conduct the study. It aligns with Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s vaccine vision. The decision allows the controversial research to proceed in the country. Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchersA controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week. It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime.

articles.title: Why A Starlink Test In Italy Has Iran's Internet Censors Worried
articles.summary: A Starlink trial in Italy connected a smartphone to the internet without mobile coverage or external antennas. The test drew attention in Iran. Iranian authorities heavily filter internet access. They imposed a near-total blackout during the January protests. A Starlink trial on an Italian hilltop connected an ordinary smartphone to the Internet without mobile coverage, a satellite dish, or an external antenna.

articles.title: ‘Horrific’ attack in Sudan, Israeli incursions in Syria intensify, most women and girls homeless in
articles.summary: A suspected drone strike killed at least 40 people in Sudan’s Blue Nile State near the Ethiopian border. UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric confirmed the toll. Most of the casualties were women and girls. Initial reports from the ground describe the attack as horrific. A suspected drone strike has left at least 40 dead in Sudan’s Blue Nile State – near the Ethiopian border - according to initial reports from the ground, according to UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric.

articles.title: Cycle of escalating attacks on civilians in Ukraine ‘must end now’
articles.summary: The Security Council addressed escalating Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian targets and infrastructure. The four-year-old war has seen a recent spate of violence. Human rights violations are now in sharp focus. Council members demanded the cycle of attacks end immediately. Escalating violence and human rights violations in the four-year-old Russia-Ukraine war are in the spotlight in the Security Council on Friday following a spate of Russian attacks against civilian targets and infrastructure in recent days.

articles.title: राहुल गांधी ने ज्ञानेश कुमार के सामने रखी शर्त, बोले- 'आप अपराधी नहीं, आपको छोड़ देंगे...'
articles.summary: राहुल गांधी ने सीईसी ज्ञानेश कुमार से इस्तीफे की मांग की। उन्होंने कहा कि कुमार अपराधी नहीं हैं और यदि वे पद छोड़ देंगे तो उन्हें माफ कर दिया जाएगा। एसआईआर के मुद्दे और सीईसी ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर कांग्रेस समेत पूरा विपक्ष मोदी सरकार पर हमलावर है. नेता विपक्ष राहुल गांधी ने सोमवार (12 अक्टूबर) को कहा कि ज्ञानेश कुमार के मैसैज आते हैं.

articles.title: जानिए क्यों विरोध की आग में झुलस रहा है अरुणाचल! चीन से जुड़ा है मामला
articles.summary: अरुणाचल प्रदेश की सियांग घाटी में 11,200 मेगावाट के प्रस्तावित परियोजना के विरोध में प्रदर्शन हो रहे हैं। स्थानीय लोग अपनी जमीन और जंगल की सुरक्षा की बात कर रहे हैं। अरुणाचल प्रदेश की खूबसूरत सियांग घाटी इन दिनों गुस्से और विरोध की आग में जल रही है. जिस सियांग नदी ने सदियों से यहाँ की जनजातियों को जीवन और आश्रय दिया है, आज वही नदी एक बड़े विवाद का केंद्र बन चुकी है.
